atoms.name: mod
atoms.rule: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: neg
atoms.rule: - a is the negation of a.
atoms.plain: - a is the negation of a.

atoms.name: list_cons
atoms.rule: a ⊲ b places integer a before the elements of list b.
atoms.plain: a ⊲ b places integer a before the elements of list b.

atoms.name: list_head
atoms.rule: a ⌃ is the first integer in a; an empty list gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⌃ is the first integer in a; an empty list gives NaN.

atoms.name: list_tail
atoms.rule: a ⌄ removes the first element of a; an empty list stays empty.
atoms.plain: a ⌄ removes the first element of a; an empty list stays empty.

atoms.name: list_length
atoms.rule: a ℒ is the number of integers in list a.
atoms.plain: a ℒ is the number of integers in list a.

atoms.name: list_append
atoms.rule: a ⊞ b joins list a followed by list b.
atoms.plain: a ⊞ b joins list a followed by list b.

atoms.name: list_sum
atoms.rule: a Σ is the sum of the integers in list a.
atoms.plain: a Σ is the sum of the integers in list a.

atoms.name: list_at
atoms.rule: a ⊙ b is element b of a, counting from zero; an invalid index gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⊙ b is element b of a, counting from zero; an invalid index gives NaN.

atoms.name: list_equal
atoms.rule: a ≍ b is true exactly when lists a and b have the same elements in order.
atoms.plain: a ≍ b is true exactly when lists a and b have the same elements in order.

domain.en: Values are lists of integers and integers. Lists may be empty; an index counts from zero.

settings.en: The preset that selects these atoms.
A recursive call repeats its step at most this many times; larger counts give NaN.
The largest number of cases in a branch definition.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: ♤₁
operators.plain: Subtract a ★₄ b from 2.

operators.name: ★₂
operators.definition: a ★₂ b = { (a ⊞ b) ⌄, if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ⊞ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], append b to a, then drop its first element; otherwise append b to a.

operators.name: ♣₃
operators.definition: a ♣₃ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♣₃ (b - 1)) ⌄, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ♣₃ (b + 1)) ⌄, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): drop the first element of the current value.

operators.name: ★₄
operators.plain: Append b to a, then count its elements.

operators.name: ♥₅
operators.plain: Take the remainder when dividing 3 by a ■₂₇ b.

operators.name: ◆₆
operators.plain: Drop the first element of a, then take its first element.

operators.name: ★₇
operators.plain: Take the remainder when dividing 3 by the length of a.

operators.name: ■₈
operators.plain: Put element b of a at the front of [1].

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♣₉
operators.plain: Take element b of a, counting from zero, then take the remainder when dividing it by 3.

operators.name: ◆₁₀
operators.plain: Test whether [1] equals a followed by b.

operators.name: ♤₁₁
operators.plain: Put a ◆₆ at the front of [1].

operators.name: ♧₁₂
operators.plain: Take the remainder when dividing 4 by element b of a.

operators.name: ●₁₃
operators.plain: Take the remainder when dividing 1 by a ★₇.

operators.name: ●₁₄
operators.plain: Take the first element of a, then add 1 to it.

operators.name: ♡₁₅
operators.plain: Take the first element of a, then subtract 0 from it.

operators.name: ★₁₆
operators.plain: Apply ♧₁₂ to a and b, then subtract 4 from it.

operators.name: ○₁₇
operators.plain: Subtract a ◆₆ from 4.

operators.name: ☆₁₈
operators.plain: Subtract a ♧₁₂ b from 0.

operators.name: ♣₁₉
operators.plain: Apply ◆₁₀ to [1] and (a without its first element).

operators.name: □₂₀
operators.definition: a □₂₀ b = { (a ♧₁₂ b) % 1, if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ♧₁₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ♧₁₂ to a and b, then take the remainder when dividing it by 1; otherwise compute a ♧₁₂ b.

operators.name: ▽₂₁
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ●₁₄ to a, then subtract 2 from it; otherwise apply ●₁₄ to a.

operators.name: △₂₂
operators.definition: a △₂₂ b = { 4 % (a ☆₁₈ b), if a ≍ [1]; a ☆₁₈ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], take the remainder when dividing 4 by a ☆₁₈ b; otherwise compute a ☆₁₈ b.

operators.name: ♥₂₃
operators.definition: a ♥₂₃ b = { [] ☆₁₈ (a ★₁₆ b), if a ≍ [1]; a ★₁₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ★₁₆ to a and b, then apply ☆₁₈ to [] and the result; otherwise compute a ★₁₆ b.

operators.name: ♡₂₄
operators.definition: a ♡₂₄ b = { (a ⊞ b) ■₈ 0, if a ≍ [1]; a ⊞ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], append b to a, then apply ■₈ to the result and 0; otherwise append b to a.

operators.name: ▽₂₅
operators.definition: a ▽₂₅ b = { (a ☆₁₈ b) - 4, if a ≍ [1]; a ☆₁₈ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ☆₁₈ to a and b, then subtract 4 from it; otherwise compute a ☆₁₈ b.

operators.name: ▼₂₆
operators.definition: a ▼₂₆ b = { [1] □₂₀ (a ⊙ b), if a ≍ [1, 2]; a ⊙ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1, 2], take element b of a, counting from zero, then apply □₂₀ to [1] and the result; otherwise take element b of a, counting from zero.

operators.name: ■₂₇
operators.definition: a ■₂₇ b = { (a ♤₁ b) % 4, if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ♤₁ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ♤₁ to a and b, then take the remainder when dividing it by 4; otherwise compute a ♤₁ b.

operators.name: ♢₂₈
operators.definition: a ♢₂₈ = { - (a ℒ), if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ℒ, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], count the elements of a, then negate it; otherwise count the elements of a.

operators.name: ♣₂₉
operators.definition: a ♣₂₉ = { [2, 3] ▼₂₆ (a ℒ), if a ≍ [1, 2]; a ℒ, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1, 2], count the elements of a, then apply ▼₂₆ to [2, 3] and the result; otherwise count the elements of a.

operators.name: ▽₃₀
operators.definition: a ▽₃₀ b = { (a ▽₂₅ b) - 3, if a ≍ [1]; a ▽₂₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ▽₂₅ to a and b, then subtract 3 from it; otherwise compute a ▽₂₅ b.

operators.name: ♢₃₁
operators.definition: a ♢₃₁ b = { [2, 3] ▽₃₀ (a ☆₁₈ b), if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ☆₁₈ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ☆₁₈ to a and b, then apply ▽₃₀ to [2, 3] and the result; otherwise compute a ☆₁₈ b.

operators.name: ◆₃₂
operators.plain: Apply ♢₃₁ to a and b, then negate it.

operators.name: ♡₃₃
operators.plain: Apply ♤₁₁ to a, then apply ♣₁₉ to the result.

operators.name: △₃₄
operators.plain: If a equals [1, 2], drop the first element of a, then apply ♡₂₄ to the result and [2, 3]; otherwise drop the first element of a.

operators.name: ○₃₅
operators.definition: a ○₃₅ b = { [1] ☆₁₈ (a ♥₂₃ b), if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ♥₂₃ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ♥₂₃ to a and b, then apply ☆₁₈ to [1] and the result; otherwise compute a ♥₂₃ b.

operators.name: ♠₃₆
operators.plain: Apply ▽₃₀ to (b with a put in front) and 2.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ☆₃₇
operators.plain: Apply □₂₀ to a and b, then apply ▽₂₅ to [2, 3] and the result.

operators.name: ◆₃₈
operators.plain: Apply ♡₁₅ to a, then add 4 to it.

operators.name: ◆₃₉
operators.plain: Apply ◆₆ to a, then subtract 3 from it.

operators.name: △₄₀
operators.plain: Take element b of a, counting from zero, then take the remainder when dividing it by 4.

operators.name: ▽₄₁
operators.plain: If a equals [1], subtract a ★₇ from 3; otherwise apply ★₇ to a.

operators.name: ○₄₂
operators.definition: a ○₄₂ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ○₄₂ (b - 1)) ♤₁₁, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ○₄₂ (b + 1)) ♤₁₁, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply ♤₁₁ to the current value.

operators.name: ○₄₃
operators.definition: a ○₄₃ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ○₄₃ (b - 1)) △₃₄, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ○₄₃ (b + 1)) △₃₄, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply △₃₄ to the current value.

operators.name: ○₄₄
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₃ to a and b, then apply △₃₄ to the result.

operators.name: □₄₅
operators.plain: Apply ♣₃ to a and b, then apply ◆₃₉ to the result.

operators.name: ◇₄₆
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₃ to a and b, then apply ★₄ to the result and [1].

operators.name: △₄₇
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₂ to a and b, then test whether the result equals [].

operators.name: ▲₄₈
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₃ to a and b, then apply ◆₃₈ to the result.

operators.name: ♥₄₉
operators.plain: Apply ♤₁ to [2, 3] and (a ♣₃ b).

operators.name: ♥₅₀
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₃ to a and b, then apply ♥₅ to the result and [1, 2].

operators.name: ♣₅₁
operators.plain: Apply ♥₅ to [2, 3] and (a ○₄₂ b).

operators.name: ◆₅₂
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₂ to a and b, then apply ♤₁ to the result and [1, 2].

operators.name: ▽₅₃
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₃ to a and b, then prepend 0 to it.

operators.name: ♠₅₄
operators.plain: Apply ♤₁ to [1] and (a ♣₃ b).

operators.name: ♣₅₅
operators.plain: Apply ♥₄₉ to a and b, then add 2 to it.

operators.name: ○₅₆
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₄ to a and b, then count its elements.

operators.name: ♢₅₇
operators.plain: Apply ♥₅₀ to a and b, then take the remainder when dividing it by 2.

operators.name: ●₅₈
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₄ to a and b, then apply ▽₅₃ to the result and 0.

operators.name: ♢₅₉
operators.definition: a ♢₅₉ b = { (a ♣₃ b) ●₅₈ 4, if a ≍ [1]; a ♣₃ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ♣₃ to a and b, then apply ●₅₈ to the result and 4; otherwise compute a ♣₃ b.

operators.name: ♠₆₀
operators.definition: a ♠₆₀ b = { [] ♥₅₀ (a ○₅₆ b), if a ≍ []; a ○₅₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [], apply ○₅₆ to a and b, then apply ♥₅₀ to [] and the result; otherwise compute a ○₅₆ b.

operators.name: ▲₆₁
operators.definition: a ▲₆₁ b = { [] ▽₂₅ (a ♢₅₇ b), if a ≍ [1]; a ♢₅₇ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ♢₅₇ to a and b, then apply ▽₂₅ to [] and the result; otherwise compute a ♢₅₇ b.

operators.name: ◇₆₂
operators.definition: a ◇₆₂ b = { 2 - (a ○₅₆ b), if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ○₅₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], subtract a ○₅₆ b from 2; otherwise compute a ○₅₆ b.

operators.name: △₆₃
operators.definition: a △₆₃ b = { [2, 3] ◇₆₂ (a ♣₅₅ b), if a ≍ [1]; a ♣₅₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ♣₅₅ to a and b, then apply ◇₆₂ to [2, 3] and the result; otherwise compute a ♣₅₅ b.

operators.name: ☆₆₄
operators.definition: a ☆₆₄ b = { 2 + (a ♢₅₇ b), if a ≍ [1]; a ♢₅₇ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], add a ♢₅₇ b to 2; otherwise compute a ♢₅₇ b.

operators.name: □₆₅
operators.definition: a □₆₅ b = { [2, 3] ▼₂₆ (a ◇₄₆ b), if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ◇₄₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ◇₄₆ to a and b, then apply ▼₂₆ to [2, 3] and the result; otherwise compute a ◇₄₆ b.

operators.name: ♡₆₆
operators.definition: a ♡₆₆ b = { [1] ♥₅₀ (a △₆₃ b), if a ≍ [2, 3]; a △₆₃ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply △₆₃ to a and b, then apply ♥₅₀ to [1] and the result; otherwise compute a △₆₃ b.

operators.name: ▲₆₇
operators.definition: a ▲₆₇ b = { [1, 2] ♥₂₃ (a ◇₄₆ b), if a ≍ []; a ◇₄₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [], apply ◇₄₆ to a and b, then apply ♥₂₃ to [1, 2] and the result; otherwise compute a ◇₄₆ b.

operators.name: ♥₆₈
operators.definition: a ♥₆₈ b = { (a ♠₆₀ b) - 3, if a ≍ [1]; a ♠₆₀ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ♠₆₀ to a and b, then subtract 3 from it; otherwise compute a ♠₆₀ b.

operators.name: ♠₆₉
operators.definition: a ♠₆₉ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♠₆₉ (b - 1)) ●₅₈ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ♠₆₉ (b + 1)) ●₅₈ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply ●₅₈ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ◆₇₀
operators.definition: a ◆₇₀ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ◆₇₀ (b - 1)) ♢₅₉ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ◆₇₀ (b + 1)) ♢₅₉ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply ♢₅₉ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ▽₇₁
operators.definition: a ▽₇₁ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ▽₇₁ (b - 1)) ○₄₄ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ▽₇₁ (b + 1)) ○₄₄ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply ○₄₄ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ○₇₂
operators.definition: a ○₇₂ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ○₇₂ (b - 1)) ▽₅₃ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 8; (a ○₇₂ (b + 1)) ▽₅₃ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 8 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -8 to 8; other values give NaN): apply ▽₅₃ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ♠₇₃
operators.plain: Apply △₆₃ to (a ♠₆₉ b) and 2.

operators.name: ▽₇₄
operators.plain: Apply ♠₆₉ to a and b, then apply ★₇ to the result.

operators.name: □₇₅
operators.plain: Apply ○₄₄ to [1, 2] and (a ♠₇₃ b).

operators.name: ♣₇₆
operators.plain: Apply ○₇₂ to a and b, then apply ●₁₄ to the result.

operators.name: ○₇₇
operators.plain: Apply □₇₅ to a and b, then take its first element.

operators.name: ♤₇₈
operators.plain: Apply □₇₅ to a and b, then apply ◆₁₀ to the result and [1].

operators.name: ○₇₉
operators.plain: Apply ●₅₈ to [2, 3] and (a ♠₇₃ b).

operators.name: □₈₀
operators.plain: Apply □₇₅ to a and b, then apply ◆₃₉ to the result.

operators.name: ♧₈₁
operators.plain: Apply ♠₆₉ to a and b, then take its first element.

operators.name: △₈₂
operators.plain: Apply □₈₀ to a and b, then apply ▲₆₁ to [2, 3] and the result.

operators.name: □₈₃
operators.plain: Apply ○₇₂ to a and b, then apply ♤₁ to the result and [1, 2].

operators.name: ♣₈₄
operators.definition: a ♣₈₄ b = { (a ♠₆₉ b) ⌄, if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ♠₆₉ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ♠₆₉ to a and b, then drop its first element; otherwise compute a ♠₆₉ b.

operators.name: □₈₅
operators.definition: a □₈₅ b = { [1] ★₂ (a ○₇₉ b), if a ≍ []; a ○₇₉ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [], apply ★₂ to [1] and (a ○₇₉ b); otherwise compute a ○₇₉ b.

operators.name: ☆₈₆
operators.definition: a ☆₈₆ b = { [2, 3] ♥₆₈ (a ♣₇₆ b), if a ≍ []; a ♣₇₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [], apply ♣₇₆ to a and b, then apply ♥₆₈ to [2, 3] and the result; otherwise compute a ♣₇₆ b.

operators.name: ▲₈₇
operators.definition: a ▲₈₇ b = { (a ♣₈₄ b) ●₅₈ 2, if a ≍ [1]; a ♣₈₄ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ♣₈₄ to a and b, then apply ●₅₈ to the result and 2; otherwise compute a ♣₈₄ b.

operators.name: ♡₈₈
operators.definition: a ♡₈₈ b = { (a ♠₆₉ b) ★₂ [1, 2], if a ≍ []; a ♠₆₉ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [], apply ♠₆₉ to a and b, then apply ★₂ to the result and [1, 2]; otherwise compute a ♠₆₉ b.

operators.name: ☆₈₉
operators.definition: a ☆₈₉ b = { (a ○₇₂ b) ⊞ [2, 3], if a ≍ [2, 3]; a ○₇₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [2, 3], apply ○₇₂ to a and b, then append [2, 3] to it; otherwise compute a ○₇₂ b.

operators.name: ●₉₀
operators.definition: a ●₉₀ b = { [] △₂₂ (a ☆₈₆ b), if a ≍ [1]; a ☆₈₆ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [1], apply ☆₈₆ to a and b, then apply △₂₂ to [] and the result; otherwise compute a ☆₈₆ b.
